test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Why are vesicles important in the functioning of the Golgi apparatus?

options.text: They carry materials to and from the Golgi apparatus
They help in forming the nucleus
They generate energy needed for packaging in Golgi apparatus

solution:
The correct answer is __**They carry materials to and from the Golgi apparatus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Golgi apparatus** functions as the central **sorting and dispatching station** for the cell's chemical products. Its primary role involves **modifying, sorting, and packaging** proteins and lipids that are synthesized in the cell.
 
• **Vesicles** are essential components of this system because they act as **transport vehicles**. They fuse with the **cis face** (receiving side) of the Golgi to deliver raw materials from the **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**.
 
• Once the materials undergo **biochemical modifications** within the **cisternae** (the flattened sacs of the Golgi), they are pinched off into new **secretory vesicles** from the **trans face** (shipping side).
 
• These vesicles then **carry the processed materials** to their final destinations, such as the **plasma membrane** for secretion outside the cell or to other internal **organelles**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike vesicles, **mitochondria** are responsible for **generating energy** (ATP), and **lysosomes** are the organelles that **digest waste** materials. Vesicles do not play a primary role in forming the **nucleus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Discovery**: The Golgi apparatus was discovered by the Italian biologist **Camillo Golgi** in **1898**. He used a unique staining technique called the **black reaction** to visualize it under a microscope.
 
• **Structure**: It consists of a series of **flattened, membrane-bound sacs** known as **cisternae**. A typical Golgi stack may contain anywhere from **three to twenty** cisternae, depending on the cell type.
 
• **Protein Modification**: One of the most important functions of the Golgi is **glycosylation**, where carbohydrate chains are added to proteins to form **glycoproteins**. This process is vital for **cell signaling** and **recognition**.
 
• **Formation of Lysosomes**: The Golgi apparatus is directly involved in the **synthesis of lysosomes**. It packages **hydrolytic enzymes** into specialized vesicles that become the cell's primary **digestive system**.
 
• **Cell Secretion**: In **glandular cells**, the Golgi apparatus is highly developed because these cells are specialized in **secreting substances** like **hormones** and **enzymes**, which require extensive packaging into **secretory vesicles**.
 
• **Plant Cells**: In **plant cells**, the Golgi apparatus is often referred to as **dictyosomes**. They play a crucial role in synthesizing **polysaccharides** like **pectin** and **hemicellulose** used in the construction of the **cell wall**.
</ul
